messages:
jamie_support: Customer reports intermittent 429s + occasional 401s when hitting /v1/generate. Happening after a spike in prefetch + embed requests. They say billing shows token charges for requests that returned 429. Can someone triage?

maria_engineer: Thanks — do we have customer request IDs and model name? pinging for quick triage.

jamie_support: model: rwd-extended-64k-v3, region: eu-west-1, keys: they rotate across two API keys (app-prod & prefetch-worker). Example request_id: req_2026-03-12_9001. Occurs around 2026-03-12T14:05Z. Billing shows tokens charged for the prefetch requests that then got 429s back.

alex_infra: Quick note: we enforce per-key and per-model RPM/TPM + concurrency. Rotating keys across same account can still hit per-model ceilings if all funnel to same capacity pool in a region. 401s suggest an auth hiccup (short-lived key rotation or clock skew).

maria_engineer: Can you paste a minimal repro curl? Also include token counts in payload.

jamie_support: paste below (redacted keys):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-extended-64k-v3","input":"<~30k tokens of context>","max_tokens":512}'
```

jamie_support: They also run a background prefetcher that does parallel embed + small generate checks (2x parallel per user) and a bulk embed job every minute.

maria_engineer: Two vectors: 1) bursty prefetch + bulk embed increases fanout and may hit per-model RPM/TPM burst windows -> 429. 2) rotating keys + short-lived tokens -> intermittent 401s (transient auth server rejects). Billing showing tokens for requests that returned 429 is expected in some cases: if the request makes it past auth and into the serving runtime and we charge for tokens consumed before throttling. We need exact request_ids and server traces to confirm.

alex_infra: From infra logs around req_2026-03-12_9001 we see: auth success -> routed -> queue -> model returned 429 with reason: model_capacity_exceeded (per-model burst). Trace: queue_wait 310ms, model_exec started, tokenize 120ms, then backpressure -> 429.

ops_bot: react :eyes: (automated note: attached trace link to internal trace viewer: https://internal.traces/req_2026-03-12_9001)

maria_engineer: That aligns: charge path happened (request passed auth and entered runtime) so token accounting recorded. For customer-facing explanation we should: a) confirm pattern, b) recommend mitigations and repro guidance.

jamie_support: Customer wants a simple mitigation checklist to reduce 429s and avoid surprise billing.

maria_engineer: Draft checklist:
- Reduce parallelism from prefetcher (limit to 1 concurrent prefetch per user)
- Add jittered exponential backoff on 429s (start 200ms, max 2s)
- Avoid bulk embed spikes; stagger jobs across minutes/hours if possible
- Pin to a lower-capacity model variant as a fallback (e.g., rwd-extended-64k-v2) when 429 rate > 5%
- Prefer single stable API key per worker process to avoid auth churn
- Collect request_ids, model, region, and token counts for any future escalations

alex_infra: Also add: consider Dedicated capacity or reserved throughput in eu-west-1 if sustained peak. Dedicated gives guaranteed concurrency and avoids per-tenant burst rejections.

jamie_support: I'll send that to the customer. Anything else to capture for an internal escalation?

maria_engineer: Yes — include these artifacts: full request_ids (both successful and 429), sample request/response headers (x-request-id, x-region, x-auth-timestamp), and timestamps. We'll run a short canary to repro: 1) run their prefetch pattern against a staging replica with traffic shaping, 2) capture per-model queue depth and per-key RPM/TPM counters.

alex_infra: For internal follow-up: engineering should check whether auth token rotation overlaps with requests (clock skew TTLs) and whether our rate limiter is attributing aggregate bursts to a single pool incorrectly when keys rotate. Filing ENGINFRA-1149.

billing_bot: Note: when a request progresses past auth and consumes compute, usage is billable even if we later return 429. If customer disputes charges, open a support credit request with exact req IDs and we'll review for exceptional credits.

jamie_support: customer asked for temporary relief while they remediate. Can we throttle them server-side or increase soft limits?

alex_infra: We can create a temporary per-tenant rate bump for eu-west-1 for up to 48h (subject to capacity). Need account ID and desired RPM/TPM. I'll coordinate with capacity ops.

maria_engineer: I'll prioritize a short repro run today and share traces. Jamie, collect the request_ids and the prefetch job schedule from the customer and attach here.

jamie_support: Will do — I'll DM the customer checklist and ask for the artifacts. Thanks all :pray:
